title: Food Safety & Hygiene
subtitle: One fact — 5 to 60 degrees — explains every rule here.
objectives: Explain why cooked rice is a special case

cards.title: One fact explains every rule in this week
cards.text: Bacteria multiply fastest at the temperature of a human body. Every food-safety rule you have ever been given follows from that.

cards.title: The danger zone is 5°C to 60°C
cards.text: Between those two numbers, bacteria grow.
points: **Below 5°C** growth slows to almost nothing.
**Above 60°C** growth stops and they start dying.
**In between is the zone.** Manila is in it all day.
**At body temperature** they can double every twenty minutes.

cards.title: Press a temperature
cards.text: Press each one. Watch both bars, and read the line underneath.

question.text: What is the temperature danger zone?

cards.title: Perishable food has about two hours, in total
cards.text: Total means cumulative, not two hours each time.
points: **Two hours out of the fridge** is the budget.
**One hour if it is above 32°C.**
**It does not reset** when you put it back.
**The fridge slows growth. It does not undo it.**

question.text: Does the two-hour clock reset when food goes back in the fridge?
question.explain: Cold slows growth; it does not reverse it.

cards.title: The two routes food poisoning actually takes
cards.text: Both are preventable with a habit rather than a product.
points: **Twenty seconds with soap** — palms, backs, between fingers, nails.
**Before cooking, after raw meat, after the bin, after the toilet.**
**Separate board for raw meat**, or wash between.
**Raw meat on the bottom shelf**, sealed, so nothing drips onto it.

cards.title: Why your fridge buys you days
cards.text: Your body runs at the exact temperature bacteria like best.
points: **37°C is the fastest growth there is.**
**Which is why an infection spreads fast** once it is inside.
**And why a fever is useful** — it is the body raising the temperature.
**Same physics, opposite direction.**

cards.title: It is a timer you cannot see
cards.text: The worst kind: no bar, no warning, and it keeps running.
points: **Two hours of budget**, spent in pieces.
**No visible countdown.**
**The penalty arrives hours later.**
**So you track it yourself.** Note the time it came out.

cards.title: A fridge does not make cold
cards.text: It moves heat out, which is a different thing and explains the warm back.
points: **A gas is compressed** and gets hot.
**Coils at the back dump that heat** into the room.
**The gas expands inside** and gets cold.
**Blocked coils mean a warm fridge.** Keep the back clear.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Danger zone: 5°C to 60°C. Fastest growth at body temperature.
Two hours total out of the fridge, one above 32°C, and it does not reset.
Twenty seconds of soap; separate boards; raw meat lowest and sealed.
Cooked rice left out is a known cause of food poisoning.

quiz.explain: Body temperature. Doubling roughly every twenty minutes.

quiz.text: Below which temperature does growth almost stop?
quiz.explain: Which is why a fridge should run at or under 4°C.

quiz.text: Above which temperature do bacteria start dying?
quiz.explain: Hot holding works for this reason.

quiz.text: How long can perishable food sit out, in total?
The two-hour clock resets each time food goes back in the fridge.
quiz.explain: The time adds up. Cold slows growth, it does not reverse it.

quiz.text: How long should you wash your hands?
Raw meat goes on which fridge shelf?
quiz.explain: Sealed, so nothing can drip onto other food.

quiz.text: Using one board for raw chicken then salad is called…
quiz.explain: Wash between, or use two boards.

quiz.text: Why is cooked rice left out overnight risky?
options: Bacillus cereus survives cooking and multiplies as it cools
quiz.objective: Explain why cooked rice is a special case

quiz.text: What should you do with warm cooked rice?
quiz.explain: Spread it out to drop through the zone quickly.
quiz.objective: Explain why cooked rice is a special case

quiz.explain: What is already there survives the freeze.
Which is why the back gets warm and must stay clear.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 3 TLE, and the most consequential week of the subject. The whole week is derived from one mechanism rather than given as a list: bacteria grow between 5°C and 60°C and fastest at body temperature, so the fridge setting, the two-hour rule and hot holding all stop being arbitrary. The interactive lets him press a temperature and see growth and safe time move together. Two points are emphasised because they are the ones usually got wrong: the two-hour clock is cumulative and does not reset, and freezing stops growth without killing anything. Cooked rice gets its own question pair because it is a real and common cause of poisoning here.
discussion: Ask for the two numbers of the danger zone.
Ask whether the two-hour clock resets.
Ask why raw meat goes on the bottom shelf.
Ask what a fridge actually does.
extension: Have him check the fridge temperature and compare it to 4°C.
Have him time twenty seconds of handwashing and see how long it feels.
misconceptions: "Freezing kills bacteria." It stops growth only.
"Putting it back in the fridge resets the clock." The time adds up.
"Rice is safe because it was boiled." The spores survive the boil.
